03 BUSINESS SESSION

A filming session for your business.

Start with one question a customer asked you yesterday. An estate agent might explain a holding deposit. A founder might talk through a hiring decision. Plain answers like these make a useful first filming session.

Plan a business shoot ↗Session rates ↗

01 SESSION NOTES

Bring four questions your customers already ask.

01

A monthly filming slot

Bring four prepared answers and record them in the same visit. We’ll agree which pieces are for LinkedIn, YouTube or your website, their finished lengths and how many edits you need.

02

A branded interview

For a corporate podcast or a customer story, send your logo and guest details ahead of time. We can plan an opening frame, name captions and a repeatable look for the next episode.

03

For agencies

Bring your producer or ask for a technician. Your brief should say who signs off, what the editor needs and whether there are multiple clients in the session. We’ll include setup and changeover time in a block quote.

02 BEFORE YOU RECORD

Good questions.

Can two clients use the room on the same day?

That can be planned as a filming block. Tell us how many people and how many changes of backdrop you need so the quote includes the resets.

Can we film in two languages?

You can record successive takes in the languages your speakers use. Specify captions and translation separately so they can be scoped and checked.

SESSION PLANNER

Put your session on paper.

Choose a starting point and save a brief. Pilot prices and dates are confirmed separately.
